target_material: TiO2 and Al2O3 nanolaminate oxide layers
summary: The study describes the deposition of TiO2 and Al2O3 nanolaminate oxide layers using atomic layer deposition (ALD) on silicon substrates. The process involves alternating pulses of TiCl4 and H2O for TiO2, and Al(CH3)3 and H2O for Al2O3. The layers are characterized using TEM and ellipsometry, showing high uniformity, flatness, and sharp interfaces. The study also explores the effects of deposition temperature on crystallization and the influence of stress on layer behavior.
evidence: Nanolaminate oxide layers consisting of TiO2 and Al2O3 have been deposited on silicon using atomic layer deposition (ALD). The deposition regime for TiO2 consisted of: 0.3 s pulse of TiCl4 and a 0.4 s pulse of H2O, interspersed with a 0.5 s purge period. The Al2O3 process conditions were: 0.4 s pulse of Al(CH3)3 and 0.4 s of pulse of H2O with a purge pulse of 0.5 s. Depositions were carried out at 200 8C.
